$schema.description: The JSON Schema this config is written against. ocel init writes the schema shipped with the CLI that created it.

allowDegraded.description: The needs this project waives rather than have a deploy refused over.

apps.description: The apps this project deploys. Left off, ocel detects one at the project root.

arch.description: The processor architecture an app's functions or container image are built for. Left off, what the provider runs the app on.

bindings.description: Whether ocel deploy hands the build the bindings of the postgres databases and kv stores the app uses, over local port forwards to them, so a page prerendered at build time can read them. Only a serverless Next app's build gets them, and only on a provider that forwards ports; any other build goes without. Left off, true. Set false to build as if no resource were provisioned.

command.description: The command that builds the app inside the image. Left off, the app's own build script runs.

context.description: The directory the image is built from, relative to the project. Left off, it is the workspace root the app belongs to.

dockerfile.description: The Dockerfile to build from. A relative path resolves against the app's directory.

compute.description: What the app runs on: serverless functions packed per route, or one container image serving everything.

domains.description: The hostnames this app is served on.

production.description: The hostnames production is served on.

domains.title: AppDomainConfig

entrypoint.description: The file the app is served from, when it is not the one ocel would detect.

folder.description: The variables folder this app reads, when it does not read the project's own.

framework.description: What a serverless app is built with, when ocel is not to read it off the app's own manifest.

health.description: How a container app is checked before it is served.

path.description: The path the check requests, off the app's own root. Any 2xx answer means up. Left off, a VPS finds the path by probing /up, /health, /healthz and / in turn and keeps the first that exists, and AWS and Google Cloud request /.

health.title: HealthConfig

maxInstances.description: The most instances of a container app run at once, however busy it is. Left off, as many as minInstances, or 1. A serverless app scales itself and takes no instance counts.

minInstances.description: The fewest instances of a container app kept running, however quiet it is. Left off, 1. A serverless app scales itself and takes no instance counts.

name.description: The app's name. It is a label of every resource the app deploys and of its preview hostname, so it is a DNS label.

path.description: The app's directory, relative to the config.

bindings.description: Resources this project declares that ocel binds instead of provisioning them itself. Keyed by resource type, then by the name the app declares. The value is "@" followed by the name a record your own infrastructure published, such as "@warehouse", and a name nothing has published refuses the deploy; or the record written inline, checked at deploy rather than provisioned, optionally keyed by the tier it serves.

domains.title: ProjectDomainConfig

edge.description: The edge in front of the origin, keyed by its identifier with its options as the value, or named alone. Omit it for the provider's default: CloudFront on AWS, and no edge on GCP or a VPS.

alb.description: Options for the Application Load Balancer edge. Everything the load balancer needs comes from the provider's own options.
alb.title: AlbEdgeOptions

api-gateway.description: Options for the API Gateway edge. Everything API Gateway needs comes from the provider's own options.
api-gateway.title: ApiGatewayEdgeOptions

cloudflare.description: Options for the Cloudflare edge. The token and account id are read from the environment.

originDomain.description: A domain in a Cloudflare zone of this account. When Cloudflare runs its worker in front of Google Cloud, the worker reaches each deployment of a serverless app on its own DNS-only hostname under it: production under the domain itself, previews under preview.<domain>. One wildcard certificate and one DNS-only record per tier are kept under it, so give it a domain nothing else uses. AWS refuses it.

tunnel.description: Reach the origin through a tunnel the origin opens to the edge, rather than at its address, so the origin takes no traffic from anything else. Cloudflare in front of a VPS box opens one.

cloudflare.title: CloudflareEdgeOptions

cloudfront.description: Options for the CloudFront edge. Everything CloudFront needs comes from the provider's own options.
cloudfront.title: CloudFrontEdgeOptions

edge.title: EdgeDescriptor
